title: Safe publication — ensuring other threads see a fully-constructed object, not a partial one

s1_definition.profdef: **Safe publication** means making an object VISIBLE to other threads in a way that guarantees they see the FULLY CONSTRUCTED object — not a partially-initialized one with default/null fields. Without safe publication, the Java Memory Model allows a thread to see a reference to an object BEFORE the constructor finishes — fields may still be zero/null. Four safe publication techniques: (1) **final fields** — guaranteed fully initialized when constructor completes (JMM freeze guarantee). (2) **volatile reference** — volatile write of the reference after construction → happens-before → other threads see complete object. (3) **synchronized block** — publish inside synchronized → memory barrier. (4) **Thread-safe collection** — `ConcurrentHashMap.put()`, `BlockingQueue.put()` have built-in happens-before. The UNSAFE way: `public static MyObj instance = new MyObj()` without volatile/final/sync → other threads may see a half-built instance.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine building a new bank branch (constructing an object). **Unsafe publication**: you put up the "NOW OPEN" sign (publish the reference) BEFORE the vault is installed, tellers hired, and computers connected. Customers walk in → no vault, no tellers → disaster. **Safe publication**: you finish EVERYTHING first (full construction), THEN put up the sign (publish via volatile/final/sync). Customers see a fully operational branch. `final` fields = vault is PERMANENTLY installed during construction — can't be seen half-built. `volatile` = the "OPEN" sign is on a special board that guarantees everyone sees the complete branch.
s1_definition.oneliner: Without safe publication: another thread sees a half-constructed object (null fields!). Safe: final fields, volatile reference, synchronized block, or thread-safe collection. Always publish AFTER full construction.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** **Safe publication** means making an object VISIBLE to other threads in a way that guarantees they see the FULLY CONSTRUCTED object — not a partially-initialized one with default/null fields. Without safe publication, the Java Memory Model allows a thread to see a reference to an object BEFORE the constructor finishes — fields may still be zero/null. Four safe publication techniques: (1) **final fields** — guaranteed fully initialized when constructor completes (JMM freeze guarantee). (2) **volatile reference** — volatile write of the reference after construction → happens-before → other threads see complete object. (3) **synchronized block** — publish inside synchronized → memory barrier. (4) **Thread-safe collection** — `ConcurrentHashMap.put()`, `BlockingQueue.put()` have built-in happens-before. The UNSAFE way: `public static MyObj instance = new MyObj()` without volatile/final/sync → other threads may see a half-built instance.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Imagine building a new bank branch (constructing an object). **Unsafe publication**: you put up the "NOW OPEN" sign (publish the reference) BEFORE the vault is installed, tellers hired, and computers connected. Customers walk in → no vault, no tellers → disaster. **Safe publication**: you finish EVERYTHING first (full construction), THEN put up the sign (publish via volatile/final/sync). Customers see a fully operational branch. `final` fields = vault is PERMANENTLY installed during construction — can't be seen half-built. `volatile` = the "OPEN" sign is on a special board that guarantees everyone sees the complete branch.

**One line to remember:** Without safe publication: another thread sees a half-constructed object (null fields!). Safe: final fields, volatile reference, synchronized block, or thread-safe collection. Always publish AFTER full construction.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The account cache service eagerly loaded accounts at startup without safe publication.** `static HashMap<String, Account> cache = loadAll()` — assigned during static initialization. Under concurrent startup: worker threads started before `loadAll()` finished. Some threads saw `cache != null` (reference published) but `cache.get("SAV2001")` returned null (entries not yet populated). NullPointerException on "Rajesh not found" for 5 seconds during startup. Fix: `volatile` reference + publish only after full load. Or: use `ConcurrentHashMap` and load into a local map first, then assign via volatile.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (Unsafe).** Thread-1: `account = new Account(...)`. CPU reorders: (1) allocate memory, (2) write reference to `account` (non-null!), (3) run constructor. Thread-2 reads `account` between step 2 and 3 → sees non-null reference but null fields!

**Step 2 (Safe — final fields).** Account has `final String id`. JMM guarantee: when constructor returns, ALL final fields are frozen and visible to any thread. Even if the reference is published unsafely, the final fields are always fully initialized.

**Step 3 (Safe — volatile).** Thread-1: constructs Account locally, then assigns to volatile reference. The volatile write creates a happens-before edge → Thread-2's volatile read sees everything that happened before the write (including all field initialization).

**Step 4 (Safe — ConcurrentHashMap).** `cache.put(key, account)` has internal happens-before guarantee → `cache.get(key)` in another thread sees the fully-constructed Account.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ UNSAFE PUBLICATION — instruction reordering ═══

  Thread-1 (CPU may reorder):
  1. Allocate memory at address 0xABC
  2. account = 0xABC         ← reference published! (non-null)
  3. account.id = "SAV2001"  ← constructor still running!
  4. account.balance = 100000

  Thread-2 reads between step 2 and 3:
  account != null (Recommended) → account.id == null! → NullPointerException!

  ═══ SAFE PUBLICATION TECHNIQUES ═══

  1. final fields:    constructor freeze → all final fields visible after new
  2. volatile ref:    volatile write → happens-before → all prior writes visible
  3. synchronized:    monitor exit → happens-before → monitor enter sees all
  4. CHM/BlockingQ:   built-in happens-before on put/take
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Safe Publication in Account Cache ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Account Service (JVM startup)                    │
  │                                                    │
  │  STEP 1: Load accounts from DB                    │
  │    Map<String, Account> local = loadFromDB();     │
  │    (local variable — not shared yet!)             │
  │                                                    │
  │  STEP 2: Publish safely                           │
  │    volatile Map<String, Account> cache = local;   │
  │    OR: concurrentCache.putAll(local);             │
  │                                                    │
  │  STEP 3: Workers start reading                    │
  │    cache.get("SAV2001") → fully-constructed (Recommended) │
  │                                                    │
  │  WRONG: cache = loadFromDB(); (not volatile)      │
  │    Workers may see cache!=null but entries missing!│
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Safe Publication Mechanisms ═══

  ┌─ final fields ──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  class Account {                                 │
  │    final String id;        // freeze guarantee   │
  │    final BigDecimal balance;                     │
  │  }                                                │
  │  JMM: constructor completes → memory barrier →   │
  │  final fields visible to ALL threads.            │
  │  Even unsafely published reference shows finals! │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ volatile reference ────────────────────────────┐
  │  volatile Account account;                       │
  │  // writer:                                      │
  │  Account temp = new Account(...); // construct   │
  │  account = temp; // volatile WRITE               │
  │  // reader:                                      │
  │  Account a = account; // volatile READ           │
  │  // happens-before: write → read → all fields ok │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Double-Checked Locking ────────────────────────┐
  │  private static volatile Singleton instance;     │
  │  if (instance == null) {         // fast path    │
  │    synchronized (lock) {                         │
  │      if (instance == null) {     // double check │
  │        instance = new Singleton(); // volatile write │
  │      }                                           │
  │    }                                             │
  │  }                                                │
  │  return instance;  // volatile read → safe!      │
  │  WITHOUT volatile: broken! (instruction reorder) │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Safe publication ensures other threads see a FULLY CONSTRUCTED object, not a partially-initialized one with null fields. Without it, the JVM/CPU may reorder instructions — publishing the reference before the constructor finishes. Thread-2 sees non-null reference → accesses fields → NullPointerException or stale default values. Four safe publication techniques: (1) final fields — JMM guarantees they're visible after constructor completes (freeze semantic). (2) volatile reference — volatile write after construction creates happens-before. (3) synchronized block — monitor exit happens-before monitor enter. (4) Thread-safe collections (ConcurrentHashMap, BlockingQueue) — built-in happens-before.

Double-checked locking for Singleton REQUIRES volatile — without it, another thread may see a non-null instance with uninitialized fields. Records in Java are ideal for safe publication — all fields are implicitly final. In banking: account cache loaded at startup must be published via volatile reference or ConcurrentHashMap. Without safe publication: workers see cache != null but entries are missing → "Account not found" errors for 5 seconds during startup → customer-visible failures.

---

keyPoints: Ensuring threads see fully-constructed object, not partial
Fix: volatile, synchronized, final fields, AtomicReference
Immutable objects are always safely published
